text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Violence breaks out in Episkopi base between bases police and residents of Trachoni village after a man is detained by the bases on charges of building illegally.
- President Glafcos Clerides lays the foundation stone for the new Nicosia general hospital.
- Episkopi scuffles. Cypriots storm a bases prison and free relatives.
- United Nations envoy Han Sung-joo announces his resignation from the post of UN special representative on Cyprus.
- Han quits, although he is "optimistic" about a meeting between President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
- Mobile phones are a goldmine for the Cyprus Telecommunications Authority, which reaps one million pounds ($2 million) from the service each month.
- U.N. envoy Han sees the two sides in Cyprus closer now to a "give and take" dialogue.

- The Interior Ministry bends the rules on building permits about once a day on average, minister Dinos Michaelides tells parliament during a debate on the construction of a hotel by the family of the former foreign minister.
- Scuffles break out in Episkopi base between base police officers and locals. Citizens managed to spring two men in detention.

- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash is to allow Greek Cypriots living in the occupied areas and their relatives to go to the Apostolos Andreas Monastery to celebrate Orthodox Easter mass on April 26. ($=0.501 pounds)
